newsitem.title: HONG KONG: TENNIS-RAFTER APOLOGISES FOR BEING DRUNK IN DAVIS CUP GAME.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-RAFTER APOLOGISES FOR BEING DRUNK IN DAVIS CUP GAME.

text.p: A remorseful Patrick Rafter apologised on Wednesday for playing a Davis Cup match for Australia last weekend while still high on alcohol.

Australian newspapers on Monday reported that Rafter, the world number 43, and Mark Philippoussis went to a nightclub in Adelaide on Saturday to celebrate taking a 3-0 winning lead over the Czech Republic in their Davis Cup world group quarter-final.
Rafter admitted that he was still feeling the effects of drink during his reverse singles match on Sunday.

"I'm glad you brought that up," said Rafter, when asked about the incident after his 2-6 7-6 6-4 win over compatriot and Davis Cup team mate Mark Woodforde in the first round of the Hong Kong Open on Wednesday.

"I cannot blame the media for what has happened -- it is totally my fault. I think the one regret I do have is giving children the wrong impression of using alcohol to win matches or be a good athlete. You just cannot do it.

"It was a rare occasion for me to go out and celebrate like that," added Rafter whose two singles victories against the Czechs helped Australia to a 5-0 win and a place in the cup semifinals against the United States.

One of his opponents in September's semifinals could be Michael Chang, the top seed here, who sailed into the second round of this tournament with a 6-0 6-1 win over wild card entrant Melvin Tong of Hong Kong.
Chang did not feature in the Americans' quarter-final win over the Netherlands at the weekend but said he was open to approaches for the semifinal.

"As far as the semifinal is concerned it will be hard to overlook Jim Courier for the first singles spot," said Chang. "As far as the second singles is concerned I am sure Tom Gullikson (the U.S. Davis Cup captain) will be getting in touch some time."
